title: Ordinary base-change ideal multiplication kernel generators
statement: Let $R,R'$ be commutative rings with a unital ring map $\rho:R\to R'$, let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, and let $M$ be any $R$-module. Put $J=\rho(I)R'$ and $N=R'\otimes_R M$, with its $R'$-action on the first factor. Suppose $(R/I)\otimes_R M$ is flat over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Write $\mu:I\otimes_R M\to M$ and $\mu_N:J\otimes_{R'}N\to N$ for multiplication and $c_N:J\otimes_{R'}N\to N\otimes_{R'}J$ for tensor symmetry. There exists an additive map $\theta_N:I\otimes_R M\to J\otimes_{R'}N$ such that $\theta_N(a\otimes x)=\rho(a)\otimes(1\otimes x)$ for all $a\in I,x\in M$, and, for every $y\in\ker\mu_N$, $c_N(y)$ belongs to the $R'$-linear span of $\{c_N(\theta_N(k)):k\in\ker\mu\}$. The pure-tensor formula determines $\theta_N$ uniquely.

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00MM, 00MN and 00M6 as used in Tag 00MO, third proof paragraph

proof.text: Construct theta by TensorProduct.liftAddHom of the explicit balanced additive pairing (a,x) -> rho(a) tensor (1 tensor x). Prove its pure-tensor formula and compatibility with multiplication and tensoring linear maps by tensor induction.

Choose the free presentation q:(M →₀ R) → M given by linearCombination of the identity family. Lift y through beta=id_J tensor baseChange(q). Its product lies in the extension of ker q by tensor right exactness and in J times the extended free module. Apply the flat quotient presentation intersection lemma.

Let P be the B-span of theta of the original multiplication kernel and W the multiplication image of beta inverse P. For f in ker q intersect IF, write f=mu_I(t) using range mu_I=IF (tensor induction and ideal-smul induction). Naturality gives mu_I((id_I tensor q)t)=q(f)=0 and mu_J(theta(t))=1 tensor f. Thus 1 tensor f is in W; span induction gives its entire base change in W.

For a in J and z in the extended ker q, beta(a tensor z)=a tensor gamma(z)=0 since gamma kills extended relations. Its multiplication is az, so ideal-smul induction puts J times the extended relation module in W. Apply the intersection inclusion to the product of the lifted y.

The base change of the free presentation module is free (tensor Finsupp basis), hence flat. By the definition of flatness, tensoring the ideal inclusion with it is injective; composing with tensor unit equivalence gives injectivity of ideal multiplication. The product of the lift lies in W, so a witness from beta inverse P with the same product equals the lift. Therefore y is in P. Tensor symmetry maps every generator theta(k) to the displayed generator, and span induction finishes.
